Base pointer r->nx has its corresponding pointer created by the r[0:1] mapping on the same construct, so it is assigned a device address and becomes an attached pointer. The device then reads r->nx->a validly; tot=10+1628=1638. Pointer not modified. Some ambiguity about attachment ordering within one construct, hence moderate confidence.

r is a scalar pointer that is the base pointer of mapped list items, so it is firstprivate. r[0:1] maps the struct and r->nx[0:1] maps the pointee; r->nx has base pointer r->nx whose storage is created in the same construct, so on entry the corresponding pointer is attached to the corresponding list item. Accessing r->v and r->nx->a on the device is then valid. No restriction is violated since the two list items do not share original storage.

Standard deep-copy pattern: r[0:1] maps the struct and r->nx[0:1] maps the pointee with base pointer r->nx, whose storage is in the new list item r[0:1]. On entry both are created, so the corresponding pointer r->nx is assigned the device address and becomes attached. The two list items do not share storage, no race, tot=10+1628=1638. The device kernel must therefore see a valid r->nx; the illegal address is a compiler or runtime bug.

The program maps r->nx[0:1] before r[0:1], so the attachment of r->nx depends on the mapping of the enclosing struct in the same construct. OpenMP 6.0 requires attachment after all storage blocks are mapped, so tot=1638 is required there. The 5.2 text only attaches if a corresponding pointer exists on entry to the region, so under 5.2 the device r->nx may keep the host address and the illegal address is arguably permitted.

r->nx[0:1] is mapped before r[0:1] on the same construct. The attached-pointer rule applies when a corresponding pointer for the base pointer r->nx exists upon entry to the region. Here r->nx lives in r[0:1], which is created by this same construct, so the rule does not clearly guarantee attachment. The device r->nx may hold the host address, so acceptance is not clearly required and the observed illegal address is not clearly a bug.
